subject: AirTide POC — success spec & perf commitments
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Samira Khan <samira@airtide.ai>, Ben Cooper <ben.cooper@airtide.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 17:32:00 -0700
Subject: AirTide POC — success spec & perf commitments

Hi Samira / Ben,

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the proposed evaluation plan, performance success criteria, and clear ownership so we can get the POC scheduled next week. Please review and flag anything missing.

1) Objective
- Validate that Redwood can serve AirTide's summarization pipeline at production latency and unit cost targets while preserving output quality on your dataset.

2) Proposed measurable success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency (p99): <= 350ms for 512-token average requests under steady-state (single shard).
- Throughput: sustained 150 requests/minute with <= 5% queuing during peak 10-minute windows.
- Cost target: <= $0.0018 per token (inference only) with recommended batching and KV cache enabled.
- Quality: ROUGE-L retention >= 0.78 vs current baseline on the supplied 500-sample test set; manual review pass-rate >= 90% on top-2 outputs.
- Stability: no crashes or OOMs across 48-hour soak with mixed request sizes.

3) Evaluation plan & artifacts
- Redwood to provide: POC template (attached), a pre-configured test harness, and a metrics dashboard (token-breakdown, latency histograms).
- AirTide to provide: sample dataset (min 500 labeled examples), definition of accept/reject labels, and a representative traffic distribution (token length histogram).
- Test cases: (a) baseline run (no caching), (b) caching + batching enabled, (c) 48-hour soak.

4) Timeline (target):
- Tue Apr 13: kickoff + infra/network check.
- Wed Apr 14: data ingest & baseline run.
- Thu Apr 15 - Fri Apr 16: perf & soak runs, iterative tuning.
- Mon Apr 19: results review + decision (pass / iterate / stop).

5) Ownership
- Redwood AE: Jonas Weber (overall coordination)
- Redwood SE: Rohan Mehta (infra, test harness, metrics)
- Redwood CS: Rafael Mendes (success criteria, QA)
- AirTide POC lead: Samira Khan (data, business acceptance)

6) Open questions for AirTide (please confirm in reply):
- Do you have any network egress restrictions (IP allowlist, proxy) for our test nodes?
- Is the 500-sample set representative of production distribution? If not, please indicate target slice.
- Any hard compliance constraints (no external logging of PII) we should enforce for the POC?

Attachments: redwood_poc_template.xlsx, network-checklist.pdf (attached).

Next step: if this looks good, we’ll lock the kickoff for Tue Apr 13 10:00 AM PT and Rohan will share a short pre-kickoff checklist.

Thanks — Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0112
From: Samira Khan <samira@airtide.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Cc: Ben Cooper <ben.cooper@airtide.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AirTide POC — success spec & perf commitments

Jonas — thanks for the recap and the clear plan. Quick confirmations and two small edits: 

- Latency target: we can accept p99 <= 350ms for 512-token avg, but please also call out p50 and p90 so we can see distribution (p50 < 120ms, p90 < 220ms).
- Throughput: our burst profile is actually 220 requests/min for short bursts (1-2 minutes) — if you can demonstrate <= 10% queuing at that burst level that would be ideal.

We’ll deliver the 500-sample labeled set by EOD Mon Apr 12. Network: yes, we have an IP allowlist and a corporate proxy; I’ll share the allowlist and proxy details in a follow-up.

Kickoff time Tue Apr 13 10:00 AM PT works for us. We’ll plan to grant scoped S3 read access for the sample dataset.

Appreciate the template — I’ll review and update comments directly in Drive.

Best,
Samira

--
Samira Khan
Head of ML Platforms, AirTide
samira@airtide.ai | +1 (617) 555-2040
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: AirTide POC — success spec & perf commitments

Internal - copying the team so ownership is clear. Notes from Samira: add p50/p90 buckets and support a 220 rpm burst with <=10% queuing. Samira will provide allowlist + proxy details and S3 read access.

Action items for SE/Infra before Tue kickoff:
- Rohan: validate our perf harness can simulate 220 rpm bursts and produce p50/p90/p99 histograms. Also confirm we can run a 48-hour soak without additional shard provisioning.
- Monica: prep the dashboard widgets (p50/p90/p99, qps, token cost, cache hit-rate) and make sure Rafael can access them for the review meeting.
- Rafael: be ready to run quality sampling (ROUGE runs + 20-manual checks) and document the manual review process.

I’ll hold the kickoff invite and share once you confirm readiness.

Jonas
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 01:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AirTide POC — success spec & perf commitments

On Sat, Apr 10, 2027 at 9:30 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference> wrote:
> Internal - copying the team so ownership is clear. Notes from Samira: add p50/p90 buckets and support a 220 rpm burst with <=10% queuing. Samira will provide allowlist + proxy details and S3 read access.

I can simulate the 220rpm burst with the harness, but I have two technical asks before kickoff: 
1) Can AirTide provide a small representative sample of production traffic (headers + token length distribution)? The 500-sample labeled set is sufficient for quality, but I need the traffic sketch to tune batching windows.
2) Please confirm whether AirTide wants KV cache persisted between runs (we currently test both ephemeral and warm-cache modes). Warm cache will significantly improve latency + cost numbers — we should surface both.

I’ll prepare the harness + pre-kickoff checklist and post it to the Drive link once ready.

— Rohan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rohan_mehta@redwood.inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@airtide.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference>

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AirTide POC — success spec & perf commitments

On Sun, Apr 11, 2027 at 1:12 AM Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.inference> wrote:
> I can simulate the 220rpm burst with the harness, but I have two technical asks before kickoff: 

Rohan — sending a small traffic sketch now (sample-traffic-sketch.csv attached) and we’ll grant S3 read access to the 500-sample labeled set this afternoon.

Regarding cache: we want both scenarios measured. Please run (a) cold start (ephemeral KV) and (b) warm-cache (persisted between runs) and label results accordingly. Warm-cache is the mode we expect in production, but we want the baseline cold-start numbers for comparison.

I’m good to proceed with Tue Apr 13 10:00 AM PT kickoff — please send calendar invite and pre-kickoff checklist.

Attachments: sample-traffic-sketch.csv, allowlist_ips.txt

Thanks,
Samira
